thread:
Ana (Support): heads-up — drafted a consolidated comms bundle for the upcoming maintenance window that impacts hosted API in eu-west and ap-southeast. want quick review before i publish to statuspage and email list.

Michael (SRE): thanks. timeline?

Ana (Support): planned window: 2026-03-25 22:00 UTC -> 2026-03-26 02:00 UTC (4h). target: kernel/driver upgrade on GPU clusters + runtime pinned-model refresh. we expect brief request throttling during model switchover, not full outage.

OpsBot: Deploy scheduled by release:redwood-runtime-v4 -> start=2026-03-25T22:00:00Z end=2026-03-26T02:00:00Z targets=[hosted-api-eu-west, hosted-api-ap-southeast] canary=15% rollback_on_error=true

Jordan (PM): high level message approved. can we add the fallback policy so customers know we have automatic variant routing?

Ana (Support): good point. included below — please check language for external copy.

Priya (Engineering): quick note: for Dedicated customers who pinned 1.2.0 -> 1.2.3 we will honor pinned versions; the runtime change won't force a model bump. Only hosted default model traffic will switch to the new runtime-optimized variant.

Liam (Eng-Release): SRE: confirm there's a canary hold if latency > 250ms p50 or error-rate increases > 1.5x baseline. That's in the rollout policy.

Michael (SRE): confirmed. canary will be 15% for 20 minutes, then 50% for 30, then full. automated rollback trigger if p50 > 250ms or 5xx rate > 1.5x. manual abort if hit either threshold during canary.

Ana (Support): copying the external comms drafts below — want final sign-off on tone and technical accuracy.

Ana (Support): STATUSPAGE DRAFT — short summary (for public, non-technical):

"Scheduled maintenance: infrastructure upgrade (Mar 25, 22:00 UTC). We will perform a routine infrastructure upgrade to improve runtime performance and reliability. During the window, some requests may experience short delays or reduced throughput. No customer data will be modified. We expect normal service to return by 02:00 UTC. If you rely on Dedicated pinned instances, you will not be forced to upgrade unless you opt in."

Ana (Support): STATUSPAGE DETAILS (for ops audience):

"What we're doing: upgrading GPU drivers and applying runtime optimizations. A small portion of traffic will be routed to an optimized model variant for verification during the canary. Impact: short-lived throttling or latency spikes during model switchover. Rollback: automated and manual rollback policies are in place; we will revert to previous binary if thresholds exceeded. Affected components: hosted API (eu-west, ap-southeast), model routing service. Not affected: private deployments, customer-managed Dedicated clusters that are pinned."

Ana (Support): EMAIL TEMPLATE (customer-facing):

"Hi <Customer>,

We're planning maintenance on Mar 25 at 22:00 UTC to upgrade our serving runtime and drivers in eu-west and ap-southeast. During this window you may experience brief increases in latency or transient throttling for requests routed to our hosted API. If you use Dedicated pinned instances, your pinned version will remain intact unless you request an upgrade.

What we're doing: kernel/driver updates, runtime performance improvements, and a controlled canary rollout.

If you have strict SLA needs during that window, reply and we'll advise on temporary routing options. We'll post real-time updates to status.redwood.inference/ and follow up once complete.

Thanks,
Redwood Support"

Jordan (PM): language looks clear. can we add an optional line about contact for dedicated customers with managed support contracts?

Ana (Support): added: "If you have a Dedicated contract with managed support, your account rep will reach out with tailored timing/options."

Priya (Engineering): suggest adding a short note about the fallback behavior for developers integrating SDKs: include suggested retry/backoff guidance (eg. 500 -> retry after 1s exponential backoff up to 3 attempts).

Ana (Support): added retry guidance to the email and status details.

Liam (Eng-Release): request: include per-region statuspage components in the post so we can update eu-west and ap-southeast independently. avoids confusing customers in other regions.

Ana (Support): done — two components and a global notice.

Michael (SRE): heads-up: if canary fails we'll trigger rollback and open incident #INC-2026-0425. Please prep a short incident tweet + status update template.

Ana (Support): drafted incident status update template (for if rollback occurs):

"We detected elevated latency during today's maintenance and have initiated rollback to the prior runtime to restore full performance. Affected: hosted API (eu-west, ap-southeast). Impact: transient increased latency for a subset of requests. We will update when rollback completes. Incident hub: link"

OpsBot: Canary stage reached 15% at 2026-03-25T22:20:00Z. Metrics: p50=190ms, 5xx=0.4% -> proceed.

Ana (Support): thanks OpsBot — pushing final publish for statuspage at 22:30 UTC unless someone objects.

Jordan (PM): no objections. please schedule statuspage and the customer email send.

Priya (Engineering): note for internal runbook: rollback steps in /runbooks/runtime-rollback.md — cross-team oncall to be notified and SRE lead to coordinate.

Ana (Support): publishing now. will post a follow-up message once live. :tada:

OpsBot: Statuspage update published at 2026-03-25T22:31:05Z (components updated: hosted-api-eu-west, hosted-api-ap-southeast, global).

Ana (Support): posted the email batch schedule: 22:35 UTC to registered contacts for eu-west and ap-southeast.

Michael (SRE): I'll be on watch for the first hour. ping me if any manual intervention needed.

Liam (Eng-Release): thanks team — leaving notes in the release ticket about the pinned-version customer list and the communications we sent.

Ana (Support): thread closing after the window unless we need to follow up with an incident update. good work everyone. :white_check_mark:
